column8: CLI storage metrics obtains physical identity through the common UnwrapEngine cursor and tests that exact result with OwnedCapability; no scoped user data read is issued by this helper.
Auth sameSystemStore compares common physical identities, then separately compares namespace metadata. Physical equality alone never grants cross-namespace store equality.
The second common physical identity is compared with the first before the namespace equality check; this is auth-store identity validation, not data capability selection.

Embedded USE reads namespace metadata through ViewMetadataForEngine, then explicitly constructs a new authorized namespace view on that namespace adapter's immediate inner engine. GetInnerEngine here is the namespace constructor input, not a generic discovery walk or a row read through a bare adapter.

Cypher reveal/decay configuration uses the common physical identity cursor and an exact native check. Query data continues through its original issued view; this helper selects the physical policy controller.

GraphQL subscription setup removes the default namespace intentionally so shared native events carry qualified database IDs; each callback derives that database before publishing its projected event. This is event-target topology, not query read recursion.

GraphQL then performs one exact wrapper hop to register the event notifier. Event callbacks preserve database provenance and use NormalEventResultProjection; normal GraphQL reads still resolve namespaced storage.

MCP storage selection first requires authorized database context, prefers the configured database-scoped factory, and only rescoping fallback constructs a new namespace over the selected namespace parent. Matching databases retain the original store.
Catalog DROP durability uses the common physical-identity owner to find Sync, then establishes metadata durability before deletion. This is a physical maintenance boundary, not a scoped data read.

The manager size-tracking wrapper declares its one topology delegation edge; mutation admission/accounting remain methods on the original wrapper. This getter supplies the common cursor, not a second traversal.
The manager wrapper explicitly declares read transparency to its parent view. It introduces no independent traversal and does not forward mutation authority with this edge.

Administrative ClearAllEmbeddings obtains the namespace via the metadata owner, saves its physical prefix, then enters that namespace adapter's immediate maintenance source. This release-defined maintenance path accepts only its explicit native/WAL shapes; it does not use the stripped adapter for ordinary data reads.

The same embedding-clear maintenance path explicitly recognizes an exact WAL wrapper before invoking the native maintenance operation, preserving the retained release durability contract. It is a fixed maintenance adapter step, not transparent read/capability recursion or a fallback after mutation error.

GetBaseStorageForManager is an explicit database-issuance API under db.mu; it removes the current namespace so DatabaseManager can create other namespaced engines. It is not used as a user data-read view.

Open removes the namespace adapter solely when registering physical event handlers that require fully-qualified IDs. SubscribeEvents is the existing event-target owner; ordinary search refresh later reads through the proper database view, and subscription failure aborts opening.
The DB helper selects native physical configuration through common UnwrapEngine plus exact OwnedCapability; it owns no separate wrapper walk or fact decoder.
Replication declares source edges for the common cursor and explicitly stops commit-owner delegation when a replicator exists, preserving the replicated commit boundary.
Replication declares its local view as the read source only; actual writes remain on ReplicatedEngine and its admission path.

Composite event-target fan-out resolves readable constituents, explicitly removes namespace views, deduplicates the shared event target, and retains all namespace transforms. This intentionally distinct event topology is not reused for reads or commits.

Embedding carry-forward asks the native physical text-policy judge whether before/after source values match. The supplied before/after bodies remain inputs; no scoped graph read is replaced by the physical result.

Namespaced HasManualSuppressions implements its own metadata forwarding through ViewMetadataForEngine on the declared child. It returns a conservative policy flag used to disable raw counts, not rows or a new count owner; overlaps TJ #1503.
Namespaced IsDecayEnabled obtains the child visibility policy through ViewMetadataForEngine. This is the namespace metadata implementation; retained TJ count forwarding/state is unchanged.

Query reveal scope selects the physical mutex owner with common identity discovery, reuses an active context lease for nested work and releases once. Database property projection remains separate and live.

Result projection resolves physical decay policy once but retains QualifiedEntityID(engine, "") for database-specific properties. It transforms supplied results and does not read arbitrary graph rows from the physical engine.
Tracing supplies its declared read-source edge to the common cursor; it performs no loop and grants no write/commit authority.
WAL supplies its declared read-source edge to the common cursor while writes continue through WAL; there is no independent wrapper walk.

readSourceIdentity delegates progression to engineCapability with identity policy. Its predicate accumulates namespace provenance and stops at captured/filtered/transaction boundaries; the one child probe recognizes a terminal wrapper, not a second cursor.
HasReadCapability is the public hint adapter over the private common read policy; it returns only a bool, so execution cannot obtain or retain a bare provider through it.

ReadWithCapability is the execution owner around common read-policy selection. readWithFallback handles refusal and preserves non-refusal errors; the caller never receives the selected provider outside its operation callback.

Managed-entity preparation uses the common physical accessor to locate the native namespace preparer registry. It does not submit/apply/forward; caller admission remains required and handled stays true on preparation error.

Temporal-index initialization uses the common UnwrapEngine physical-identity owner only to acquire the native maintenance lifecycle. Node emptiness/backfill work remains on the original scoped engine and actual schema owner; this lookup does not grant a native visible-read or mutation fallback.
UnwrapEngine itself is the physical-policy adapter over engineCapability. Its predicate recognizes terminal/self wrappers; all progression and cycle/depth handling belong to that single cursor.
Replay asks the common physical accessor for its lifetime lease target while graph writes retain the entry-specific NamespacedEngine.
Replay deliberately replaces an existing namespace with entry.Database before recovery apply, avoiding double-prefixing; the one explicit hop is recovery rescoping.

WAL undo explicitly replaces the current namespace with the entry database before applying the inverse operation. This is recovery rescoping over the original base wrapper, not a hidden data-read fallback.
Recovery restore uses the physical accessor solely to enter the native semantic property-restore owner. No read provider or user visibility decision is selected.

Recovery foreign-property marking obtains a native helper lifetime lease and walPropertySource lock before changing provenance. Physical identity discovery does not bypass a mutation wrapper to stage a user write.
